itineraries.title: Salt of the Earth - 5 Day Itinerary
editorial: While the salt flats of Uyuni are the primary attraction in Bolivia, your journey will most likely start by landing in Santa Cruz (unless you take a bus from Chile). From there you take a short but tumultuous flight to Sucre and an overnight bus to Uyuni. Spend at least a day in Uyuni before exploring the salt flats as the altitude may take a bit to acclimate to.
What if we had more time?
If we had more time, we’d certainly visit Laguna Colorada, the red salt lake home to flamingoes.

days.title: Day 1 - Santa Cruz + Sucre
editorial: We didn’t leave Santa Cruz airport on Day 1 as our flight to Sucre was shortly after landing (see Day 5 for things do in Santa Cruz).
Sucre is the most unassuming national capital we’ve been to. The infrastructure is at least a couple of decades behind it’s neighbours, but the people are decidedly nicer.
Get a spot near the bus terminal as there isn’t much else to do in Sucre. The bus to Uyuni is an overnight ride. Oh, and if you haven’t already, buy medicines for altitude sickness!

days.title: Day 2 - Uyuni
editorial: We arrived in Uyuni in the wee hours of the morning and walked to our hotel. It’s a quaint little town that feels far-removed from the more westernised parts of Latin America. Unsurprisingly, it’s reminiscent of the Andean towns like Ollantaytambo in neighbouring Peru.
Food is a bit hard to come by, as restaurants have limited operating hours. We visited Tika, a cute cafe with a pace of service that ensures you will devour your meal by the time it gets you!
The rest of the day was spent battling altitude sickness.

days.title: Day 3 - Uyuni
editorial: Finally, the main event is here. We did a day tour of the salt flats. The 3-day / 2-night tour that includes Laguna Colorada is the more popular option, but we didn’t feel up for long hours on the road especially after a long bus ride. Back when we went, there was no 2-day / 1-night option.

Depending on when you go, you will witness the magnificence of the dry salt flats and / or the mirror reflection of it’s wetter avatar. Either way, you will have surreal pictures and videos to say the least.
There’s a separate stargazing tour that you can take on a moonless night. Unfortunately, our visit coincided with a full moon.

days.title: Day 4 - Uyuni
editorial: Our last day in Uyuni was spent lazing around town until it was time for our bus. A word of caution: check with the locals about the bus terminal. Google Maps led us astray and we almost missed our ride! A cab driver came to our rescue and didn’t rip us off.

As sweet as Bolivians are, their economic hardships are inescapable. At times, we felt like there was sadness writ on many faces in Uyuni. More than once, we encountered child labour (which we later found out was legal in Bolivia!).

days.title: Day 5 - Sucre + Santa Cruz
editorial: And so, we trudge back to Santa Cruz by road and air. If time permits, check out Plaza 24 de Septiembre (the main square), Catedral de Santa Cruz (next to the main square), and Mercado Los Pozos for local cuisine.
